title: Conditional Moves [cmov]
description:
## Conditional Moves
You know `set` stores 0 or 1. But sometimes you want to move a FULL value conditionally - without jumping.

`cmov` moves a value only if the condition is true. Otherwise it does nothing.

```asm
cmp rdi, 10
cmovg rax, rsi    ; rax = rsi ONLY if rdi > 10
```

All the same suffixes as jumps:
- `cmove` - move if equal
- `cmovne` - move if not equal
- `cmovg` - move if greater
- `cmovl` - move if less
- `cmovge` - move if greater or equal
- `cmovle` - move if less or equal

### Why?
No branch = no branch misprediction = faster. CPUs hate unpredictable jumps.

```asm
; With jumps (slow if unpredictable):
cmp rdi, rsi
jg .use_rdi
mov rax, rsi
jmp .done
.use_rdi:
mov rax, rdi
.done:

; With cmov (always fast):
mov rax, rsi
cmp rdi, rsi
cmovg rax, rdi    ; overwrite only if rdi > rsi
```

---
## Assignment:
Write a function `max_val` that takes two numbers in `rdi` and `rsi` and returns the larger one in `rax`. Use `cmov` - no jumps allowed!
setupCode:
section .data
    pass_msg db "PASS", 10
    pass_len equ $ - pass_msg
    fail_msg db "FAIL", 10
    fail_len equ $ - fail_msg

section .text
    global _start
starterCode:
max_val:
    ; return the larger of rdi and rsi. No jumps!
    ret
runHarness:
_start:
    mov rdi, 5
    mov rsi, 3
    call max_val
    cmp rax, 5
    jne .fail
    mov rdi, 2
    mov rsi, 8
    call max_val
    cmp rax, 8
    jne .fail
    mov rdi, 7
    mov rsi, 7
    call max_val
    cmp rax, 7
    jne .fail
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, pass_msg
    mov rdx, pass_len
    syscall
    jmp .exit
.fail:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, fail_msg
    mov rdx, fail_len
    syscall
.exit:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
